name: Pfarrkirche St. Jakob am Arlberg
kurzbeschreibung: The baroque Saint Jakob Parish Church is the oldest parish in the Arlberg region and a traditional spiritual milestone on the Tyrolean Way of Saint James.
preis: Free entry (contributions toward maintenance and sacred art conservation welcomed)
oeffnungszeiten: Open daily year-round from approx. 08:00 to 18:00
beschreibung:
Overview

The delightfully situated Saint Jakob Parish Church (Pfarrkirche Sankt Jakob am Arlberg) in the eponymous district of Sankt Anton am Arlberg is revered as the oldest mother parish of the upper Stanzer Valley. Documented as early as the 13th century, the church served for centuries as the religious and community heart for dispersed alpine farming settlements near the Arlberg Pass. Its present baroque appearance dates from the mid-18th century, when a new nave was constructed while incorporating the older Gothic bell tower. As a historic pilgrimage site, the church serves as an essential milestone for walkers on the famous Tyrolean Way of Saint James (Jakobsweg).

Route & Requirements

From central Sankt Anton, a tranquil footpath follows the rushing Rosanna mountain river or winds along the sunny panoramic high trail to Sankt Jakob. Inside, the church welcomes visitors with a harmonious baroque interior, adorned with lovely ceiling frescoes depicting the life and miracles of church patron Saint James the Greater. The intricately carved high altar and delicate side shrines reflect the profound faith of generations of alpine villagers. A peaceful stroll through the surrounding churchyard offers resting benches with breathtaking views of the rugged limestone crests of the Lechtal Alps and Verwall mountain range. Paths are flat and paved, making the visit gentle and relaxing.

Visit & Arrival

The church welcomes worshipers and culture lovers daily throughout the year from 08:00 to 18:00. Entrance is free of charge. Public transportation is simple and convenient: the international railway station at Sankt Anton am Arlberg is served by Railjet and EuroCity trains from across Europe. From there, local bus line 3 reaches St. Jakob Kirche in just a few minutes. Motorists take the S16 Arlberg expressway to Sankt Anton; in the hamlet of Sankt Jakob, designated parking spaces are situated within short walking distance of the church entrance.

Tips

Pilgrims and long-distance hikers can have their pilgrim passports stamped inside the church with the official Jakobsweg stamp. Highly recommended is combining your visit with a hike along the Arlberg section of the Jakobsweg downvalley toward Schnann or into Sankt Anton to explore the Ski & Local Heritage Museum documenting the history of alpine skiing. During summer, lush meadows invite quiet contemplation.
